page.title: Best smartwatch for iPhone with two weeks of battery life under $200 (2026)
page.h1: Best smartwatch for iPhone that lasts two weeks or more, under $200 (2026)
page.desc: Which iPhone-compatible smartwatches under $200 really last two weeks? Reviewers' day counts with the always-on display on and off, set against Amazfit's ratings for the Active Max, Bip Max, Bip 6 and Active 2.
page.answer: Short answer. The best smartwatch for iPhone with two weeks of battery life under $200 is the Amazfit Active Max ($169.99): in Basic Tutorials' review it lasted about 10 days with the always-on display on and 13–14 days with it off. The 14-day Bip 6 lasted 8 days in Droid.tools' review.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Active Max: 10 reviewer days ÷ 25 rated days = 40% of the rating with the always-on display on. With it off, 10 + 3 to 4 = about 13–14 days, the only figure here that reaches two weeks.
  • Bip 6: 8 ÷ 14 = 57% of the rating with the display on. 14 − 8 = 6 days short of two weeks.
  • Active 2 (Round): 6 ÷ 10 = 60% of the rating. 14 − 6 = 8 days short.
  • Bip Max: Amazfit's own always-on rating is 7 ÷ 20 = 35% of its typical-use rating, and its heavy-use rating is 10 ÷ 20 = 50%.
  • Charges a month: Bip 6 at 8 days: 30 ÷ 8 ≈ 4 charges. Active Max at about 13.5 days with the display off: 30 ÷ 13.5 ≈ 2 charges.
  • What the extra money buys: $169.99 − $79.99 = $90 for about 5–6 more days per charge (13–14 vs 8).
If you want…Buy
A real two weeks between charges, with the screen waking on a wrist raiseActive Max, always-on display off
An always-on screen and the longest runActive Max (about 10 days with a reviewer's settings)
The lowest price, and you can charge once a weekBip 6
The biggest screen (2.07-inch) at about $100, relying on Amazfit's ratingBip Max

{buy:amazfit-active-max}

Two weeks with the screen on or off: what reviewers counted

Amazfit's "up to" figures assume light use. The Bip Max page footnote defines typical use this way: a static watch face, heart rate every 5 minutes, three 30-minute GPS workouts a week, 150 notifications a day and 5 minutes of screen time a day. The always-on display is not part of that test. Amazfit's own Active Max support guide says turning it on "greatly reduces the battery life".

  • Active Max: Philipp Briel (Basic Tutorials, February 2026) wore it with the always-on display, continuous blood-oxygen measurement and sleep tracking on, and it "lasted a good 10 days". He adds that switching the always-on display off gives "another three to four days". the5krunner estimated continuous GPS at about 40 hours, against Amazfit's claimed 64 hours, at minimum brightness with the always-on display off.
  • Bip 6: Luiza Mosneagu (Droid.tools) got "eight days, to be precise" with several GPS workouts, heart-rate monitoring and the always-on display. Carlsen Martin (Gizbot) got up to eight days with similar settings and says it reaches 14 days only on more conservative settings.
  • Active 2 (Round): Carlsen Martin (Gizbot) got about six days per charge with the always-on display, raise-to-wake and auto-brightness on.
  • Bip Max: There is no reviewer day count yet. Amazfit rates it 20 days typical, 10 days heavy and 7 days with the always-on display.

On an iPhone: all four watches use the Zepp app, which needs iOS 15.0 or later in the US App Store. All four are on the Zepp OS 5 list, so they can reply to WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Messenger, Slack and Discord chats through Zepp Messenger, which needs a free Beeper account. Zepp describes sending SMS from the watch only for Android users, and iMessage replies are not possible because Beeper connects iMessage only on a Mac. So replies don't separate these watches; battery does. {buy:amazfit-bip-6}

Not recommended

Amazfit Active 2 (Round). It costs $99.99, the same as the Bip Max, but Amazfit rates it at half the battery (10 days against 20). Gizbot's reviewer got about six days with the always-on display on. Even its best-case rating falls short of two weeks.

notes: Confirmed today (2026-11-08): Bip 6 $79.99 and 'Up to 14 days battery life' (storecheck on the Amazfit US store). Basic Tutorials (Philipp Briel, 27 Feb 2026): 'lasted a good 10 days' with always-on display, continuous SpO2 and sleep tracking; 'another three to four days' with it off. Droid.tools (Luiza Mosneagu): 'eight days, to be precise'. Gizbot Bip 6 (Carlsen Martin): up to eight days with always-on display; 14 days with more conservative settings. Gizbot Active 2 (Carlsen Martin, standard round model): about six days with always-on display, wrist-raise wake and auto-brightness. Amazfit support: 'greatly reduces the battery life'. Zepp OS 5 list includes all four watches; Beeper needed for iOS replies; WhatsApp, Messenger, Telegram, Signal, Slack and Discord listed. App Store: 'Requires iOS 15.0 or later'. All the arithmetic in the after-section checks out (40%, 57%, 60%, 35%, 50%, ≈4 and ≈2 charges, $90, 5–6 days, 6 and 8 days short).
